# Phase 1: the techniques and the planner

Part of the [`ci-doctor`](../../SKILL.md) hub. What [Phase 1](../phases/phase-1-map-the-repo.md) needs from the guide and the reference READMEs, copied from them so the phase runs where only the skills are installed. Each part links its source.

## The techniques

Every technique in guide sections 2–17 and 21, by section, each with when it applies and when to skip it. Mark each that applies and bears on the measured limiter, and read its section only then.

- **[2. Runners, Blacksmith, and the cost of getting fast](../../../../docs/pages/02-runners-blacksmith-and-the-cost-of-getting-fast.md)**
  - [Choosing a provider and runners](../../../../docs/pages/02-runners-blacksmith-and-the-cost-of-getting-fast.md#choosing-a-provider-and-runners): **Applies when:** The plan picks a provider, or sizes or resizes runners, on any CI platform. **Skip when:** The baseline shows neither runner cost nor runner size bearing on the limiter.
  - [When jobs wait to start](../../../../docs/pages/02-runners-blacksmith-and-the-cost-of-getting-fast.md#when-jobs-wait-to-start): **Applies when:** The slowest tenth of jobs wait minutes for a runner, or queue time is a large share of the PR wait. **Skip when:** Queue time is seconds, as on most repos.
  - [Why we recommend Blacksmith](../../../../docs/pages/02-runners-blacksmith-and-the-cost-of-getting-fast.md#why-we-recommend-blacksmith): **Applies when:** The repo runs GitHub Actions on GitHub-hosted or self-hosted runners, and the baseline shows where queue, compute or setup time goes. **Skip when:** The repo is off GitHub Actions, or the user declines the move: the plan stays on the current runners.
  - [Setting up Blacksmith](../../../../docs/pages/02-runners-blacksmith-and-the-cost-of-getting-fast.md#setting-up-blacksmith): **Applies when:** The user approved a move to Blacksmith. **Skip when:** The plan stays on the current runners.
  - [Getting fast costs money and time first](../../../../docs/pages/02-runners-blacksmith-and-the-cost-of-getting-fast.md#getting-fast-costs-money-and-time-first): **Applies when:** The plan prices its own optimization period: sweeps, replays, measurement runs, bisects and debugging. **Skip when:** The plan changes nothing that runs in CI.
- **[3. Workflow anatomy](../../../../docs/pages/03-workflow-anatomy.md)**: **Applies when:** The repo is on GitHub Actions and its workflow lacks a plan job that gates the others, or a single result job that checks them. **Skip when:** The workflow already gates every job on a plan and checks them in one result job.
- **[4. Run only what a change can reach](../../../../docs/pages/04-run-only-what-a-change-can-reach.md)**
  - [Drafts and concurrency](../../../../docs/pages/04-run-only-what-a-change-can-reach.md#drafts-and-concurrency): **Applies when:** PR workflows run while a PR is a draft, or a draft event or an old rerun can cancel the newest head's run. **Skip when:** Every job already skips drafts and concurrency groups keep ready PRs, drafts, reruns, manual runs and merges apart.
  - [A selector built from a real dependency graph](../../../../docs/pages/04-run-only-what-a-change-can-reach.md#a-selector-built-from-a-real-dependency-graph): **Applies when:** A pnpm workspace's TypeScript tests, named `.test.ts` or `.test.tsx`, run in full on every PR. **Skip when:** Tests in other languages or named another way, whose jobs keep running in full until a selector maps them, and a Turborepo or Nx repo, which starts with its own affected run.
  - [Turborepo and Nx: their own affected runs first](../../../../docs/pages/04-run-only-what-a-change-can-reach.md#turborepo-and-nx-their-own-affected-runs-first): **Applies when:** The repo uses Turborepo or Nx and selects nothing today. **Skip when:** The repo uses neither.
  - ["Near" selection for an integration-heavy server](../../../../docs/pages/04-run-only-what-a-change-can-reach.md#near-selection-for-an-integration-heavy-server): **Applies when:** Every integration test boots the whole server, so the import graph says everything reaches everything, and main's sweeps run the full set as the safety net. **Skip when:** The import graph already narrows the selection, or no sweep on main covers what "near" leaves out.
  - [CI file changes run only the jobs they touch](../../../../docs/pages/04-run-only-what-a-change-can-reach.md#ci-file-changes-run-only-the-jobs-they-touch): **Applies when:** A selector exists and a workflow or composite-action edit selects every job. **Skip when:** There is no selector yet, or CI file edits already run only the jobs they touch.
  - [Other narrowing](../../../../docs/pages/04-run-only-what-a-change-can-reach.md#other-narrowing): **Applies when:** Real-container tests, packaging or a Rust service run on every PR whatever it changes. **Skip when:** None of those runs on every PR.
  - [Verify the selector like production code](../../../../docs/pages/04-run-only-what-a-change-can-reach.md#verify-the-selector-like-production-code): **Applies when:** A selector, or a change to one, is proposed. **Skip when:** Selection isn't changing.
- **[5. Tiers: what runs where](../../../../docs/pages/05-tiers-what-runs-where.md)**: **Applies when:** Checks too slow or costly for every PR could run on merges, on main's server runs or in a sweep instead. **Skip when:** No sweep has yet been shown to run every check it would take off PRs ("Releasing what the sweep checked", below).
  - [Moving heavy tests to the right tier](../../../../docs/pages/05-tiers-what-runs-where.md#moving-heavy-tests-to-the-right-tier): **Applies when:** Expensive files run on every PR: bounded model checks, large-fixture, long-history or large-dataset tests, wide grids, full oracle corpora. **Skip when:** No PR test is expensive enough to tie to the inputs it proves.
  - [Replaying recorded sessions](../../../../docs/pages/05-tiers-what-runs-where.md#replaying-recorded-sessions): **Applies when:** An end-to-end path depends on an outside tool whose live runs are slow, paid or nondeterministic, such as an agent harness calling a model. **Skip when:** Every outside dependency already has a fast local fake at the boundary you test.
  - [Cron is not a scheduler you can trust](../../../../docs/pages/05-tiers-what-runs-where.md#cron-is-not-a-scheduler-you-can-trust): **Applies when:** GitHub's scheduled runs carry checks, such as sweeps or main-only jobs. **Skip when:** The repo has no scheduled or main-only jobs.
  - [One issue for a red main, and a bisect with a budget](../../../../docs/pages/05-tiers-what-runs-where.md#one-issue-for-a-red-main-and-a-bisect-with-a-budget): **Applies when:** A sweep on main runs checks that PRs skip, so a failure has to be traced to a merge. **Skip when:** Main has no sweep.
  - [Releasing what the sweep checked](../../../../docs/pages/05-tiers-what-runs-where.md#releasing-what-the-sweep-checked): **Applies when:** Any PR coverage would move to a sweep, or a release or deploy should ship only what the sweep checked. **Skip when:** PRs keep all their coverage.
- **[6. Reuse work by its real inputs](../../../../docs/pages/06-reuse-work-by-its-real-inputs.md)**
  - [Task runners and their remote caches](../../../../docs/pages/06-reuse-work-by-its-real-inputs.md#task-runners-and-their-remote-caches): **Applies when:** The repo has a workspace task runner, or caches task results today. **Skip when:** The repo would adopt a runner only for its cache and section 4's selection replay hasn't come first.
  - [Checking a cache on another task runner](../../../../docs/pages/06-reuse-work-by-its-real-inputs.md#checking-a-cache-on-another-task-runner): **Applies when:** Replays come from a runner with declared inputs, such as Turborepo, Nx, Bazel or Gradle. **Skip when:** The runner tracks what each task reads, as Vite+ does, or nothing is cached.
  - [A remote task cache, with tests as tasks](../../../../docs/pages/06-reuse-work-by-its-real-inputs.md#a-remote-task-cache-with-tests-as-tasks): **Applies when:** Task results are shared through a remote cache: on Vite+ as written, on other runners through the table above. **Skip when:** No task results are shared across machines.
  - [Setting up the remote task cache on Cloudflare, step by step](../../../../docs/pages/06-reuse-work-by-its-real-inputs.md#setting-up-the-remote-task-cache-on-cloudflare-step-by-step): **Applies when:** The plan self-hosts Vite+'s remote cache on Cloudflare, with the trust policy already decided. **Skip when:** Another runner's cache, a hosted cache, or the trust policy still open.
  - [Rust: reuse passes and binaries separately](../../../../docs/pages/06-reuse-work-by-its-real-inputs.md#rust-reuse-passes-and-binaries-separately): **Applies when:** The stack has Rust. **Skip when:** It has none.
  - [Setup caches on Blacksmith](../../../../docs/pages/06-reuse-work-by-its-real-inputs.md#setup-caches-on-blacksmith): **Applies when:** Installs and toolchain setup take job time: on Blacksmith with its sticky disks, elsewhere with the Actions cache fallback. **Skip when:** Setup isn't where the job time goes.
  - [Not worth caching](../../../../docs/pages/06-reuse-work-by-its-real-inputs.md#not-worth-caching): **Applies when:** A cache is proposed for sub-second generation, npm tarballs, Rust sccache in CI or another layer. **Skip when:** No new cache layer is proposed.
- **[7. Shards, runners and billing](../../../../docs/pages/07-shards-runners-and-billing.md)**
  - [Shards from measured time, not file count](../../../../docs/pages/07-shards-runners-and-billing.md#shards-from-measured-time-not-file-count): **Applies when:** Tests run, or should run, across several shards, and each file's time on main is recorded. **Skip when:** There are no per-file times yet.
  - [Work stealing over cache-key claims](../../../../docs/pages/07-shards-runners-and-billing.md#work-stealing-over-cache-key-claims): **Applies when:** Fixed shards from measured time are in place and runner speed still varies, measured on its own. **Skip when:** Fixed shards aren't in place yet.
  - [Independent lanes](../../../../docs/pages/07-shards-runners-and-billing.md#independent-lanes): **Applies when:** A shard runs its workers in rounds, so a lane waits for the slowest. **Skip when:** Each lane already starts its next task the moment it finishes.
  - [Size runners from the work and the bill](../../../../docs/pages/07-shards-runners-and-billing.md#size-runners-from-the-work-and-the-bill): **Applies when:** Per-job CPU over at least three runs, the high tail included, shows a job sized wrongly, or tiny selections pay a big runner's minimum minute. **Skip when:** Fewer than three runs agree.
  - [Shorten the critical path before buying cores](../../../../docs/pages/07-shards-runners-and-billing.md#shorten-the-critical-path-before-buying-cores): **Applies when:** Jobs wait for upstream jobs before starting their own setup, or test binaries run one after another. **Skip when:** The critical path is a single job's own work.
- **[8. A faster test harness](../../../../docs/pages/08-a-faster-test-harness.md)**: **Applies when:** A server with a heavy runtime per test file, such as workerd under Vitest. **Skip when:** The runtime's startup and bundling are a small share of each test file's time.
- **[9. Workspace tooling](../../../../docs/pages/09-workspace-tooling.md)**
  - [The commands](../../../../docs/pages/09-workspace-tooling.md#the-commands): **Applies when:** A TypeScript workspace, adopting one command at a time where a named duplicate pass or a measured bottleneck justifies it. **Skip when:** The repo's existing commands show neither: keep them as they are.
  - [One type check, no duplicate passes](../../../../docs/pages/09-workspace-tooling.md#one-type-check-no-duplicate-passes): **Applies when:** A framework's diagnostics or type-aware lint run as a separate compiler pass. **Skip when:** One type pass already covers them.
  - [Every file in a project, enforced](../../../../docs/pages/09-workspace-tooling.md#every-file-in-a-project-enforced): **Applies when:** One consolidated type check covers the workspace through project references. **Skip when:** Each project is checked on its own.
  - [Type results follow content across worktrees](../../../../docs/pages/09-workspace-tooling.md#type-results-follow-content-across-worktrees): **Applies when:** Several worktrees type-check the same projects on one machine. **Skip when:** Each machine has one checkout.
  - [Type-aware lint where it pays](../../../../docs/pages/09-workspace-tooling.md#type-aware-lint-where-it-pays): **Applies when:** The linter has type-aware rules, and local checks run them on every file while many agents check at once. **Skip when:** The linter has no type-aware rules.
  - [Keep lint config out of the test config](../../../../docs/pages/09-workspace-tooling.md#keep-lint-config-out-of-the-test-config): **Applies when:** Lint settings live in the config the tests load, so a lint edit invalidates test transforms and cached test keys. **Skip when:** Tests already load their own config.
  - [Custom lint rules that guard the shortcuts](../../../../docs/pages/09-workspace-tooling.md#custom-lint-rules-that-guard-the-shortcuts): **Applies when:** The repo takes shortcuts a rule can guard: build tasks with explicit inputs, seeded property tests, restricted runtimes, package boundaries. **Skip when:** It takes none of them.
  - [No build before checking or testing](../../../../docs/pages/09-workspace-tooling.md#no-build-before-checking-or-testing): **Applies when:** Workspace packages must be built before checks or tests can import them. **Skip when:** They already resolve to source.
  - [Generated files](../../../../docs/pages/09-workspace-tooling.md#generated-files): **Applies when:** Checks, tests or builds consume generated files. **Skip when:** Nothing is generated.
  - [Find existing code before writing more](../../../../docs/pages/09-workspace-tooling.md#find-existing-code-before-writing-more): **Applies when:** Agents write code in the repo; the saving is a warm local one, not a measured CI one. **Skip when:** No agents write code here.
  - [Pin everything, share the tool](../../../../docs/pages/09-workspace-tooling.md#pin-everything-share-the-tool): **Applies when:** Node, pnpm or shared tool versions float, or the static workflow stops at its first failing command. **Skip when:** They are pinned and every command reports.
  - [If you use Effect](../../../../docs/pages/09-workspace-tooling.md#if-you-use-effect): **Applies when:** The stack uses Effect. **Skip when:** It doesn't.
- **[10. Slow tests: the method](../../../../docs/pages/10-slow-tests-the-method.md)**
  - [Find them from CI's own records, not intuition](../../../../docs/pages/10-slow-tests-the-method.md#find-them-from-cis-own-records-not-intuition): **Applies when:** Test time bears on the measured limiter, and CI's records give per-file durations. **Skip when:** There are no per-file records yet: recording them comes first (section 13).
  - [Name the wait before changing anything](../../../../docs/pages/10-slow-tests-the-method.md#name-the-wait-before-changing-anything): **Applies when:** A file past 10 s, or one that ends its shard, is on the inventory. **Skip when:** The inventory is empty.
  - [Keep what each test proves](../../../../docs/pages/10-slow-tests-the-method.md#keep-what-each-test-proves): **Applies when:** Any test is made faster. **Skip when:** No test changes.
  - [Measure honestly](../../../../docs/pages/10-slow-tests-the-method.md#measure-honestly): **Applies when:** A before and after, or any timing comparison, is reported. **Skip when:** Nothing is compared.
- **[11. Flakes](../../../../docs/pages/11-flakes.md)**: **Applies when:** CI's records show tests that failed and then passed, or jobs that passed on rerun. **Skip when:** The records show no failed-then-passed tests or jobs.
  - [Cause, symptom, fix](../../../../docs/pages/11-flakes.md#cause-symptom-fix): **Applies when:** A failure's symptom matches one below, or a fixture forks, spawns, binds a socket, runs Git or uploads a stream. **Skip when:** None of the tests start processes, open sockets or run Git.
- **[12. Budgets, health and spend](../../../../docs/pages/12-budgets-health-and-spend.md)**: **Applies when:** The plan sets job or run budgets, a spend cap or a health report, or a baseline compares spend across windows. **Skip when:** None of those is proposed or measured.
- **[13. Records: evidence of what ran](../../../../docs/pages/13-records-evidence-of-what-ran.md)**: **Applies when:** CI can't show which test files ran, or per-file timings are missing. **Skip when:** The repo already logs every executed file and its time on each run.
  - [Collecting from the API without losing runs](../../../../docs/pages/13-records-evidence-of-what-ran.md#collecting-from-the-api-without-losing-runs): **Applies when:** A baseline, audit or report is built from the provider's API. **Skip when:** The evidence comes only from the repo's own records.
- **[14. Local speed, and many agents on one machine](../../../../docs/pages/14-local-speed-and-many-agents-on-one-machine.md)**
  - [Fast local feedback](../../../../docs/pages/14-local-speed-and-many-agents-on-one-machine.md#fast-local-feedback): **Applies when:** Agents or people wait on local checks. **Skip when:** Local checks already run only what covers the change.
  - [The local runner contract](../../../../docs/pages/14-local-speed-and-many-agents-on-one-machine.md#the-local-runner-contract): **Applies when:** A local runner runs a selected list of tests, such as `test:cached` or one you write. **Skip when:** Local runs take no selection.
  - [Sharing one machine](../../../../docs/pages/14-local-speed-and-many-agents-on-one-machine.md#sharing-one-machine): **Applies when:** Several agents or worktrees run tests on one shared machine. **Skip when:** Each machine runs one checkout.
- **[15. The agent workflow around CI](../../../../docs/pages/15-the-agent-workflow-around-ci.md)**: **Applies when:** Agents open, ready and merge the repo's PRs. **Skip when:** People run the PR workflow; keep the repo's trigger and merge policy until the user approves a change.
  - [How we run a review](../../../../docs/pages/15-the-agent-workflow-around-ci.md#how-we-run-a-review): **Applies when:** A repo adopts the review gate and has no review process of its own for what the gate requires. **Skip when:** The repo's own review already decides who reviews and how, or it doesn't gate CI on a review.
  - [Running a slow-test campaign with parallel agents](../../../../docs/pages/15-the-agent-workflow-around-ci.md#running-a-slow-test-campaign-with-parallel-agents): **Applies when:** The slow-file inventory is long enough to split among agents, and the harness runs them in parallel, each in its own worktree. **Skip when:** The harness can't run parallel agents, or one agent can work the inventory.
- **[16. Standing automations](../../../../docs/pages/16-standing-automations.md)**: **Applies when:** A repeated, read-only or deterministic follow-up would otherwise be done by hand, and the user says yes to its schedule. **Skip when:** The user hasn't said yes: a manual, read-only follow-up is the default.
- **[17. Keeping agent knowledge from going stale](../../../../docs/pages/17-keeping-agent-knowledge-from-going-stale.md)**
  - [Where knowledge lives](../../../../docs/pages/17-keeping-agent-knowledge-from-going-stale.md#where-knowledge-lives): **Applies when:** Agents work in the repo and the plan's findings go into their instructions. **Skip when:** No agents work in the repo.
  - [What keeps it fresh](../../../../docs/pages/17-keeping-agent-knowledge-from-going-stale.md#what-keeps-it-fresh): **Applies when:** The repo keeps lessons or a tried-and-dropped register that agents read. **Skip when:** No agents work in the repo.
- **[21. Optimize all of your graphs](../../../../docs/pages/21-optimize-all-of-your-graphs.md)**: **Applies when:** A workspace has several packages or a CI run of several jobs, and an edit selects, rebuilds or waits on more than it touches. **Skip when:** One package and one job, where there is no graph to shape.
  - [Package dependencies, declared and checked](../../../../docs/pages/21-optimize-all-of-your-graphs.md#package-dependencies-declared-and-checked): **Applies when:** A workspace's packages import each other, and nothing but review stops a new import across them. **Skip when:** A single package, or a build tool that already refuses undeclared edges, such as Bazel's `deps`.
  - [Export paths: what an edit triggers](../../../../docs/pages/21-optimize-all-of-your-graphs.md#export-paths-what-an-edit-triggers): **Applies when:** A shared package has a root barrel, or a few wide entry points, and an edit to one module selects most of its importers. **Skip when:** Each package is small enough that every importer uses most of it.
  - [Layers and folders inside a package](../../../../docs/pages/21-optimize-all-of-your-graphs.md#layers-and-folders-inside-a-package): **Applies when:** A package's folders import each other in both directions, or "near" selection climbs from a small edit to most of a package. **Skip when:** Packages are small, flat, or already split along their folders.
  - [Workspace tasks](../../../../docs/pages/21-optimize-all-of-your-graphs.md#workspace-tasks): **Applies when:** A task runner caches tasks, and a small edit misses more of the cache than it should. **Skip when:** No task runner, or nothing is cached.
  - [CI jobs](../../../../docs/pages/21-optimize-all-of-your-graphs.md#ci-jobs): **Applies when:** A run's result waits on jobs that wait on others, or on runners. **Skip when:** One job.
  - [Measure the graphs](../../../../docs/pages/21-optimize-all-of-your-graphs.md#measure-the-graphs): **Applies when:** Before tightening any graph above, and after each change to one. **Skip when:** Nothing above applies.
  - [Adopt them in a repo that has none](../../../../docs/pages/21-optimize-all-of-your-graphs.md#adopt-them-in-a-repo-that-has-none): **Applies when:** Graphs 1–3 aren't declared yet. **Skip when:** They are.

## 18. Tried and dropped

From [docs/pages/18-tried-and-dropped.md](../../../../docs/pages/18-tried-and-dropped.md). What was tried and dropped, and what would have to change before trying again.

See what we tried and dropped, the evidence that ruled each out, and what would have to change before it's worth trying again.

**When** is the week of our six-week effort in which we tried or decided it. **Outcome** says what kind of evidence ruled it out: *measured*, *modelled* or *replayed* and rejected; *shipped then replaced* or *removed*; *folded into another change*; or *rejected on principle*. The last column says what replaced it, or what would have to change before trying again. Our rows' evidence was our own PRs and runs, which this public copy leaves out; your register keeps an Evidence column, as the [`ci-read-what-was-tried`](../checks/ci-read-what-was-tried.md) check's template has.

| When | Idea | Outcome | What we saw | Lesson | Replaced by, or retry when |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Week 1 | Local-only pre-merge checks, no CI | Shipped then replaced | Runner spend stopped for the interval; no controlled total-cost or reliability comparison was recorded | No CI bill isn't a measured saving | Dedicated-runner CI |
| Weeks 1–2 | Many tiny parallel jobs (39) | Measured and rejected | Faster completion, but substantially more rounded runner usage than packed jobs | Include setup and billing rounding in the model | Fewer, fuller jobs; retry only if setup and rounding stop dominating |
| Week 2 | Arm runners for JS tests | Measured and rejected | Tests ran ~30% slower and three integration files failed, despite a ~37% lower minute price | Unit price isn't service price | Arm stays useful for native builds; retry when the same tests run as fast and pass |
| Week 2 | Specialized checkout cache (a mirrored checkout) | Rejected | The existing checkout was already cheap, and the mirror bills storage | Measure fixed work before adding persistent storage | Repos whose checkout is several GB |
| Week 2 | Docker layer caching for intentionally clean, verified builds | Rejected | Conflicted with the clean-build contract; verified images were already reused by content tag | Reuse only independently verified complete images | — |
| Weeks 2 and 4 | Dependency disk containing only `node_modules` | Measured and rejected | Installation and postinstall work remained, because their markers lived in the store outside the disk | Preserve and verify the complete installation, including toolchain, store markers and workspace links | The complete-install disk ([section 6](../../../../docs/pages/06-reuse-work-by-its-real-inputs.md#setup-caches-on-blacksmith)) |
| Week 2 | Vitest's isolation, pools and module caches | Measured and rejected | Shards spent almost all their time in the tests themselves | Time was in single slow files and tests that wait, not in the runner | Retry when import or transform time is a real share of a shard |
| Week 2 | One job per test file, or per part of one | Measured and rejected | Each part used about one core in four | Per-job setup and minute rounding dominate | Never, while setup is billed per job |
| Week 2 | Vitest `--changed` / import-graph selection over a whole-Worker harness | Replayed and rejected | 494 of 1,035 files for one edit; median 19% fewer files but ~0 billed minutes saved; 13 missed disk readers; slow to select | Imports don't describe integration coverage | Near selection plus sweeps, then explicit coverage edges (section 4) |
| Week 2 | Automatic input tracking for every build | Measured and rejected, for builds | `spawn EBUSY` on our dev platform; subprocess reads were a correctness concern too | Explicit inputs, with a lint rule for completeness | Retry when tracking works on every dev platform; tests use it today (section 6) |
| Week 2 | Time-balanced shards before splitting giant files | Modelled and deferred | Can't help while one file is longer than a shard's share | Split first, then balance | Shipped once the long files were split (section 7) |
| Week 2 | 9 workers on 8 vCPU | Measured and rejected | About 1.5–1.8× as long as 6 workers, with timing failures | Spare CPU isn't spare capacity | — |
| Week 2 | Ordinary tests after every merge | Folded into another change | A closed proposal, superseded before it was measured | Batch the broad check, keep merge types | Sweeps (section 5) |
| Week 3 | Halving a timer-heavy job's runner | Measured and rejected | Each file 30–45% slower, and CPU saturated, for a small saving | Keep burst headroom | — |
| Week 3 | Shared-machine Docker admission | Shipped then removed | Dedicated CI replaced the shared machine; removing the forwarding socket hung most runs, so it stayed | A removal can depend on something no one recorded | — |
| Week 3 | Human-picked extra slow/sandbox coverage on PRs | Shipped then removed | Extra catches were all flakes; zero failures in 81 slow jobs | Broad pre-merge coverage needs observed value | Changed files on PRs, the rest in sweeps |
| Week 4 | Rebuilding macOS release binaries less often | Modelled and rejected | Every macOS job was a real release; each binary embeds its version, and the service pairs only with its own release | Unchanged source doesn't make an old binary valid for a new release | Fewer releases, or a deliberately redesigned version contract |
| Week 4 | A test clock ten times faster to bring a shard file under 90 s | Measured and rejected | One case had too little real time for its work and flaked in CI | Shorten a deadline only where the real time left covers the work on a busy runner | Real-clock deadlines sized to the work |
| Week 4 | Long-lived binaries and tarballs as artifacts | Shipped then replaced | Exhausted artifact storage and broke sweeps | Retention follows usefulness | Cache handoffs and short retention; a later outage showed what still depended on artifacts (section 19) |
| Week 4 | Staging-connected recording/proof extension | Shipped then reverted | Landed, then reverted, and its remaining connections removed | A closed or reverted experiment doesn't establish why it was rejected | Deterministic recording and replay remained; the reason for the revert isn't recorded |
| Week 4 | Reusing imported state across server files | Measured and rejected | Leaks failed 8 tests in 6 files on a second run | A green run can't prove isolation | — |
| Week 4 | Lower Go memory limits for the type checker | Measured and rejected | 50–80% slower, <2 GB saved | The live heap is the floor | Go backend only; since replaced by tsrs (section 9) |
| After week 6 | A local adapter package that ran tsrs-lint in tsgolint's place, through a package-manager override | Shipped then replaced | Faster type-aware lint with the same findings, but an override, a symlink and a peer rule to keep in step with each upgrade | Delete a workaround once the tool does the job, and show the job still runs | Vite+ 1.7, which runs tsrs itself (section 9) |
| Week 4 | Trimming what TypeScript loads, to speed up checking | Measured, kept, no speed-up | Declarations loaded fell; checking time didn't move | Scheduling set the time, not load | Retry when the checker is load-bound |
| Week 4 | Splitting test files further to shorten shards | Rejected | Each file adds a harness start | Split only what's past the per-file limit | — |
| Weeks 4–5 | Whole-tree hash test-pass cache | Shipped then replaced | Replayed 0 of 4,872 file runs over 7 sweeps | Key by what each task reads | Tracked-read tasks (section 6) |
| Weeks 4–6 | Rust in CI: lld/mold, 256 codegen units, opt-level tweaks, one combined test binary, sccache, shared compile with packaging | Measured and rejected | Negligible, slower, or lost fidelity; the combined binary broke 3 tests | Profile before tuning the compiler | — |
| Undated | Shared Cargo target dir across worktrees | Rejected | Returned the wrong worktree's binary as fresh | mtime freshness isn't content | One `target/` per worktree, plus sccache |
| Weeks 4–6 | Shared runtime / watch mode across test files | Measured and rejected | <10% a file; broke isolation (module state, alarms, DB names) | Share compilation, not state | — |
| Weeks 4–6 | A resident incremental bundler | Measured and rejected | About halved bundling, but held 1.7 GB idle and got an agent OOM-killed | Memory is a cost on a shared box | Bundle once per input state (section 8) |
| Week 4 | Deep property tests on every PR | Shipped then moved | Ended last, repeating fixed seeds the PR run covered | Depth belongs in the sweep | Sweep runs with fresh seeds (section 5) |
| Week 4 | Cache only tiny packages on one shard | Measured and rejected | Five CI trials saved no billed minutes, because the cached work was too small | Compare lookup and restore cost with the work removed | Broader caching after independent lanes (section 6) |
| Week 4 | Cutting the rest of a harness's start: no proxy, lazy wasm, a code cache, a shared or pooled runtime | Measured and rejected | What could go while each file keeps its own runtime was a few percent of test time | Tests need the proxy, and a shared runtime breaks per-file state | The server bundle loading less at start, a production change |
| Week 4 | Cutting a shard's fixed costs: the web build, test bundles, the module cache | Measured and rejected | Each was seconds a shard; the module cache's key took the lockfile and configs, so almost every full run started cold | Check a cache's key against how often its inputs change | A key that survives lockfile churn |
| Week 4 | The claim queue's fixed share, claims between runs, batches cut by time alone | Modelled and in CI; replaced | A slower machine ran past the others' share; per-batch runs paid start-up again; time-only batches ignored each file's start | Model the slowest machine and per-file start | Share and file-start cost went in |
| Week 5 | Merging a declaration and cached-check spike wholesale | Folded into another change | Closed unmerged; project-level caching was built locally first | A closed spike isn't a rejected technique | — |
| Week 5 | Caching sub-second generation | Shipped then removed | Replay took two to four times as long as the work | Cache overhead can beat the work | Ordered direct generation that writes only changes |
| Week 5 | npm tarball cache | Measured and rejected | The restore cost more than it saved | Measure the restore | — |
| Week 5 | The remote cache duplicated in the Actions cache | Shipped then removed | Hid whether remote reuse worked at all | Keep one copy, so hits are attributable | The remote cache alone |
| Week 5 | Cached execution in rounds, two workers per group | Measured and replaced | Workers waited for slow group members | Rounds idle workers | Independent lanes, one server file per task |
| Week 5 | One private cache path per lane | Measured and replaced | The path itself entered every key, so nothing replayed across sweeps | Anything in the environment can enter a key | Shared storage with per-invocation status |
| Week 5 | Raising cache concurrency further | Rejected | The buffers exceeded the Worker's memory allowance | Concurrency is bounded by memory, not only by the CPU | A shared byte budget instead of fixed buffers |
| Week 5 | Several broad local cached suites at once on a shared machine | Measured and replaced | Warm single runs didn't survive several together: timeouts and resets | A shared-host result, not a rule against broad checks | Fewer slots and focused local selection |
| Week 5 | Four server files per cached task | Measured and rejected | Fewer launches, but longer shards and much more idle time at the end | Indivisible groups lose to lanes | — |
| Week 5 | Fully async SQL test transport, or deferred writes | Measured and rejected | Changed completion order and visibility, breaking clock-driven cases | Optimize transport while preserving the caller's contract | The synchronous socket (section 10) |
| Undated | Low-priced external sandboxes as runners | Measured and rejected | About a third slower on average, and flaky | Don't trade every-PR wait for cents | — |
| By week 2 | Long-lived test boxes | Rejected | Idle time billed up to a 30-minute timeout | Lifecycle economics matter | — |
| — | A separate "fast" local command | Rejected on principle | — | Make the default command fast | — |
| — | A test mode in production code | Rejected on principle | — | One code path; a period differs by setting | — |
| — | Making a fake slow to mimic a real rate limit | Rejected on principle | — | Prove behaviour at the limit instead | — |
| — | Widening a production API to remove a test's last wait | Rejected on principle | — | The API is the product | — |

Rows that were folded into another change, or closed before anyone measured them, aren't failed optimizations. Don't count them as performance failures unless evidence shows one.

## 20. Thresholds cheat sheet

From [docs/pages/20-thresholds-cheat-sheet.md](../../../../docs/pages/20-thresholds-cheat-sheet.md). The source repo's starting values, as examples, not targets.

Look up the starting values we used for slow files, shards, budgets and flakes, as examples to derive your own from.

Our starting values, as examples from one repo. Don't adopt them as targets: derive yours from your own bottlenecks and comparable runs.

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| Slow test file | > 10 s in CI |
| Split a file | > ~90 s, by subject (ordinary shard files; container files have a 10-minute file timeout) |
| Shard target | 75 s of tests per worker, 6 workers, ≤ 16 shards |
| Shard length | ≤ ~2 min elapsed including setup, on a provider that rounds per job; p95 warning at 110 s |
| Full PR run / small run budget | 5 min / 3 min |
| Job budget | p95 + 15%, rounded up to 5 s |
| Small runner | `server_files + other/10 ≤ 6` → 2 vCPU, 2 workers |
| Work stealing | ~50% of estimated work fixed; queued batches of whole groups summing ~60 s of estimated work |
| Near-selection fan-in cutoff | 20 importers |
| Rust pass reuse window | 30 h (sweep refreshes at 20 h) |
| Flake priority bump | 3 in 7 days |
| Flake close | ≥ 7 quiet days and 50 clean executions (7 clean executions for sweep-only and job-level issues) |
| In-CI retry | 1, in-process; 0 locally and in proof repeats |
| Runner resize | Only when 3 runs agree on CPU |
| Re-estimate container test time | Off by > 20% |
| Local test slots | `max(2, floor(cores / 4))`, unless `TEST_SLOTS` is set |
| Wait hints | Files > 10 s |
| Like-for-like noise band | ~±40% on single comparisons in our CI; measure your own |
| Records collector | ≤ 1,500 API calls a night, counted as made; keep 1,000 spare |
| Startup gate | Bytes allocated at module load, 15% over the measured value, for each deploy bundle; CPU only as a gross ceiling |
| Build-once fixture | Only where setup is at least ~⅓ of the file's time |
| Unix socket path | ≤ 107 bytes on Linux, ≤ 103 on macOS: check before binding |
| Interactive proof wait | Completion evidence, polled every 0.2 s; stillness only for the first prompt, or as a logged fallback after 20 s |
| Persisted-wait replay test | First pass sleeps 10 min, replay 1 s |

## 4. Run only what a change can reach

From [docs/pages/04-run-only-what-a-change-can-reach.md](../../../../docs/pages/04-run-only-what-a-change-can-reach.md). Selection with Turborepo or Nx.

### Turborepo and Nx: their own affected runs first

**Applies when:** The repo uses Turborepo or Nx and selects nothing today. **Skip when:** The repo uses neither.

A repo on Turborepo or Nx already has package-level selection built in: `turbo run <task> --affected` and `nx affected -t <task>`. When the repo selects nothing today, turn that on before writing a selector. Both compare against a base commit, so check that CI fetches enough history to reach it and passes the right base for a PR (check the installed version's docs: the flags and defaults have changed between releases).

- **It's package-level.** A change selects every task of its package and of the packages depending on it, through the tool's own graph. Edges that graph can't see still need declaring: root config, files read from disk across packages, generated code. Unknown inputs should select everything, as above.
- **Verify it like a selector:** replay recent PRs and compare what it ran against what they needed ([below](../../../../docs/pages/04-run-only-what-a-change-can-reach.md#verify-the-selector-like-production-code)).
- **Don't replace a finer selector with it.** Where the repo already selects by test file, keep that: a package graph replacing semantic selection missed tests in 74 of 100 replayed PRs (above). Our planner in [`templates/plan/`](../../../../templates/plan/README.md) reads pnpm workspaces only, so in a Turborepo or Nx repo it's for a later pilot, not a first step.

## 5. Tiers: what runs where

From [docs/pages/05-tiers-what-runs-where.md](../../../../docs/pages/05-tiers-what-runs-where.md). The release checklist each shipping path is mapped to, before any PR coverage moves to a sweep.

### Releasing what the sweep checked

**Applies when:** Any PR coverage would move to a sweep, or a release or deploy should ship only what the sweep checked. **Skip when:** PRs keep all their coverage.

The release and deploy rows above rest on a few steps. Map each one to your own release mechanism before you defer any PR coverage to a sweep. [`templates/github/README.md`](../../../../templates/github/README.md#release-integration-checklist) maps steps 2 to 7 to the scripts; step 1 is `ci.yml` plan's first step.

Two conditions come first:

- **One complete sweep, proven.** Before you route any check off PRs or turn on the release gate, show one sweep that ran every deferred check, and list each deferred check with the evidence of its success. A sweep can report success on an unchanged commit after running only its plan, and the release helper matches a passing sweep by workflow, branch, title and shipped content. Neither tells you which deferred checks were wired in or ran, so the gate must match the sweep's coverage policy, or a verified coverage record for it, including when a sweep inherits an earlier run's result. [`release-checked.ts`](../../../../scripts/sweeps/release-checked.ts)' `sweeps.requiredJobs` names the jobs a release counts on: add each before its check leaves PRs. Checks against live systems (staging, external tools) need their own freshness rule.
- **Every shipping path waits.** Leave required coverage on PRs until every path that ships checks a successful full run at the exact release commit, or at a proven-equivalent input identity. Define what happens on a missed, failed or stale sweep, and on a manual promotion. A direct deploy binds to a checked commit or artifact digest. A repo whose deploys follow every merge, or that has no usable release gate, keeps PR coverage.

The steps below are ours, for npm packages with optional native children. Other artifacts need their own: for a Python wheel or sdist, the build metadata, the resolved build inputs and an install and smoke test in a clean environment; for a container, the image digest.

**A container image, deployed by digest.** Our deploys built their container images until we named each by its digest in the deploy config, so a deploy builds no image and needs no Docker. A record beside each digest holds the hash of the inputs it was built from, and a test fails a PR that changes those inputs without a new digest. A separate CI job builds only the images whose inputs changed, twice on fresh storage, checks the two builds match, pushes the image under a tag named by its inputs, checks the registry's digest is the one it built and fails until the PR records it. A tag is never pushed again. The deploy tool checks each named digest exists before it uploads, so a missing one fails the deploy and the live version stays. We didn't measure the time saved; the change took the image build out of every deploy and limited cold builds to changed images. [Caches](../../../cache-ci/references/caches.md#who-may-write-a-cache) says why the build uses fresh storage.

1. **Reject unpublished snapshot dependency URLs** in ordinary PRs, sweeps and releases. Permit them only in explicitly targeted manual experiments. [`scripts/sweeps/`](../../../../scripts/sweeps/) has the guard; run it right after the plan checks out.
2. **Run the content-equality guard before tagging or publishing:** the shipped files must match what a passing sweep checked.
3. **Build every release platform fresh.**
4. **Pack once, then install each tarball with the plain package manager alone** (npm, for us) and validate the installed artifacts.
5. **Publish optional platform packages before the parent package** that depends on them.
6. **On a retry, publish only the versions still missing,** from the same tarballs. Never overwrite a published version.
7. **After publishing, advance production to the sweep's checked commit,** with an ancestor or fast-forward check.

## 6. Reuse work by its real inputs

From [docs/pages/06-reuse-work-by-its-real-inputs.md](../../../../docs/pages/06-reuse-work-by-its-real-inputs.md). Guide section 6's cache table, and the trust policy a shared cache needs.

### Task runners and their remote caches

**Applies when:** The repo has a workspace task runner, or caches task results today. **Skip when:** The repo would adopt a runner only for its cache and section 4's selection replay hasn't come first.

We used Vite+. Most workspace task runners have a remote cache, and each technique in this section has an equivalent setting in them. Start from the runner your repo already has; adopting one only for its cache needs the selection replay in section 4 first.

| Technique | Vite+ (`vp run`) | Turborepo | Nx | Bazel | Gradle |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Tests as cached tasks** | Test groups defined as tasks in `run.tasks` (ours: [`test-tasks.ts`](../../../ci-runners/scripts/test-tasks.ts)); tasks cache by default | A `test` task in `turbo.json`; tasks cache unless `cache: false` | A `test` target with `"cache": true`, usually in `targetDefaults` | Test targets cache by default (`--cache_test_results=auto`) | The built-in `Test` task is cacheable; a custom task opts in with `@CacheableTask` |
| **Keying by real inputs** | Automatic: it records file reads, missing-file probes and directory listings. Narrow with `cache.input` globs and `!` exclusions | `inputs` globs per task (`$TURBO_DEFAULT$` plus exclusions); `globalDependencies` for files every task reads | `inputs` and `namedInputs` (`sharedGlobals` for workspace-wide files), plus `externalDependencies` and `dependentTasksOutputFiles` | Each action's declared sources, dependencies and tools. Tools outside the workspace aren't tracked | Annotated task inputs, with `@PathSensitive(PathSensitivity.RELATIVE)` so checkouts at other paths share keys |
| **Environment in the key, run-specific values out** | `cache.env` keys a variable; `cache.untrackedEnv` passes one without keying it | `env` / `globalEnv` key a variable; `passThroughEnv` / `globalPassThroughEnv` pass one unkeyed; `envMode: "strict"` hides the rest | `{ "env": "NAME" }` and `{ "runtime": "<command>" }` inputs; variables not listed aren't keyed | `--action_env` keys a variable; `--incompatible_strict_action_env` (on by default) fixes `PATH`, so machines share hits | A value declared with `inputs.property(…)` is keyed; an environment read the task doesn't declare isn't, so declare every one that changes the result. Keep absolute paths out of inputs |
| **Outputs to restore** | Automatic write tracking, or `cache.output`; `output: []` replays a pass without restoring files | `outputs` globs; logs always replay, so `outputs: []` suits a test pass | `outputs` per target | Each action's declared outputs, from the content-addressed store | Declared `@OutputFile` / `@OutputDirectory` |
| **PRs read; only main's CI writes** | `VP_REMOTE_CACHE=read` on PRs, `read-write` on main. The remote mode isn't in Vite+'s public docs yet; [`cache/remote/`](../../../../cache/remote/README.md) documents what we run | `--cache=local:rw,remote:r` on PRs (or `TURBO_CACHE` with the same value) | No client switch for a self-hosted server: give PRs a token the server refuses writes for (the spec's 403 for a read-only token). Nx Cloud has read-only tokens | `--remote_upload_local_results=false` on PRs | `push` on the remote `HttpBuildCache` set only in main's CI. Gradle's example pushes from any CI (`isCiServer`); narrow it to main |
| **Checking replays** (a sampled uncached rerun compared with the replay) | `vp run --no-cache` on a sample; ours is `test-lanes.ts --verify-hits <n>` | Rerun the sample with both caches off (`--cache=local:`); compare `--dry=json` hashes | `NX_SKIP_NX_CACHE=true` reruns cached tasks; add `NX_SKIP_REMOTE_CACHE=true` so the probe neither reads nor writes the remote | `--noremote_accept_cached --cache_test_results=no`, with uploads off; compare two runs' `--execution_log_compact_file` logs | `--rerun-tasks --no-build-cache`; `-Dorg.gradle.caching.debug=true` prints each key |
| **Trust and signing** | No signing in the protocol. Our Worker: token digests, read tokens for PRs, OIDC writes from main | `remoteCache.signature: true` with `TURBO_REMOTE_CACHE_SIGNATURE_KEY` signs artifacts (HMAC-SHA256), and an artifact that fails the check is a miss. The key is shared, so a valid signature says who holds the key, not which run wrote it | Self-hosted: bearer tokens, no signing. Nx Cloud offers end-to-end encryption (`NX_CLOUD_ENCRYPTION_KEY`): privacy, not provenance | No signing. Blobs are addressed by their digest, but action-cache entries aren't signed; Bazel's docs suggest letting only CI write | No signing; HTTP Basic credentials. Gradle's docs recommend that CI populates the cache and developers only load from it |

Sources, checked November 2026: Vite+ [task caching](https://viteplus.dev/guide/cache) and [run config](https://viteplus.dev/config/run); Turborepo [configuration](https://turborepo.dev/docs/reference/configuration), [`run` options](https://turborepo.dev/docs/reference/run), [environment variables](https://turborepo.dev/docs/reference/system-environment-variables) and [remote caching](https://turborepo.dev/docs/core-concepts/remote-caching); Nx [inputs](https://nx.dev/docs/reference/inputs), [caching](https://nx.dev/docs/concepts/how-caching-works), [environment variables](https://nx.dev/docs/reference/environment-variables) and [self-hosted caching](https://nx.dev/docs/kb/self-hosted-caching); Bazel [remote caching](https://bazel.build/remote/caching), [cache-hit debugging](https://bazel.build/remote/cache-remote) and the [command-line reference](https://bazel.build/reference/command-line-reference); Gradle [build cache](https://docs.gradle.org/current/userguide/build_cache.html), [cache debugging](https://docs.gradle.org/current/userguide/build_cache_debugging.html), [incremental build](https://docs.gradle.org/current/userguide/incremental_build.html) and the [command line](https://docs.gradle.org/current/userguide/command_line_interface.html).

**Self-hosting.** Turborepo's server implements its [Remote Cache API](https://turborepo.dev/docs/openapi); community servers include [one on Cloudflare Workers with R2](https://github.com/AdiRishi/turborepo-remote-cache-cloudflare). Nx's implements its [OpenAPI spec](https://nx.dev/docs/kb/self-hosted-caching#open-api-specification), set with `NX_SELF_HOSTED_REMOTE_CACHE_SERVER` and `NX_SELF_HOSTED_REMOTE_CACHE_ACCESS_TOKEN`. Bazel takes an HTTP or gRPC cache, such as [bazel-remote](https://github.com/buchgr/bazel-remote), set with `--remote_cache`. Gradle takes any HTTP server that answers GET and PUT, or Gradle's build cache node.

**The trust design carries over.** [`cache/remote/`](../../../../cache/remote/README.md)'s design works in front of any of these servers. The server stores only each token's SHA-256 digest, so its config holds no secret. PRs get a read token. Writes come only from main's CI, identified by GitHub's OIDC token (its repository, event and ref), so there's no write secret to leak. A self-hosted server for any runner can make the same checks before it stores an entry. Whichever you use, authentication says who wrote an entry, not that the work was honest ("Trust", below).

### Trust

- **Trust:**
  - **Authentication isn't provenance.** A cache writer can supply a forged pass or build output for inputs main reads. OIDC proves who wrote an entry, not that the computation was honest. Before sharing results, list every writer and every release or deploy path that consumes them, then pick and document a policy: shared writes from protected main only, with branches in isolated namespaces; equivalent independent verification; or no remote reuse for anything that ships. Sampling hits fresh (below) catches some faults but doesn't establish provenance. Our own setup accepted broad writers as known development debt. The example in [`cache/remote/`](../../../../cache/remote/) ships the narrow policy instead, writes only from main's pushes; widen it only as a recorded decision: [its README](../../../../cache/remote/README.md#trust-decide-who-may-write-what-main-replays) holds the writer list, the consumer list and the policy choice.
  - CI reads with a secret and writes with a GitHub OIDC token. Our policy lets main pushes, same-repo PRs and branch manual runs write: the broad debt above. The narrow policy we recommend, and the one `cache/remote/` ships, writes only from main's pushes, with every PR and dispatch reading. Forks run fresh.
  - Developers read and write with personal credentials.
  - Read failures are misses, and upload failures don't fail a passed task.

## 14. Local speed, and many agents on one machine

From [docs/pages/14-local-speed-and-many-agents-on-one-machine.md](../../../../docs/pages/14-local-speed-and-many-agents-on-one-machine.md). What a local runner of selected tests must do before its green means they ran.

### The local runner contract

**Applies when:** A local runner runs a selected list of tests, such as `test:cached` or one you write. **Skip when:** Local runs take no selection.

`test:cached` is a selection plus a runner. A runner that just takes the selected list can report green when tests didn't run. Ours does all of the following. [`scripts/local/`](../../../../scripts/local/) ships only the selection, so make sure whatever runner you write or use meets every point:

- **Form stable groups from the whole ordinary suite, then filter,** so a group's key doesn't depend on the selection. Local grouping is separate from CI's.
- **Bound concurrent tasks** from the machine's file-slot cap.
- **Fall back to every ordinary test** if selection fails.
- **Validate explicit paths,** and refuse ambiguous substring matches.
- **Serialize callers** that share a summary or cache directory. Tag each invocation and round, and reject foreign or missing summaries.
- **Account for every selected file** as replayed, passed, failed, interrupted or not run, and fail when execution is incomplete.
- **`--no-cache` turns off reads and writes** in both the local and remote tiers.
- **Optionally re-run a sample of hits uncached** to check soundness. Never count a replay as a fresh flake observation.

Let the repo supply its own database and generated-file setup; the contract doesn't need our stack.

## Selection planner

From [templates/plan/README.md](../../../../templates/plan/README.md). The selection planner's inputs and its limits.

### The rules, in order

1. **CI files** (`ci.yml`, called workflows, `.github/actions/`), with `--near`: both revisions are parsed as YAML and compared block by block. A changed job runs itself plus everything that waits on it, through `needs` or the `wait-for-jobs` action; a changed action runs its callers. The plan, the result, the top level, an unknown job or an unparseable file select everything.
2. **Root scripts** are classified by their callers: only tests → those tests; one CI step's tool → that job; production code → like an edit to that package; deciding selection or execution (`runScripts`), or named by the root manifest outside its tools → everything. Unknown scripts fail toward everything.
3. **Shared inputs and the checks themselves** → everything.
4. **Docs, agent guidance and ignore files** → no tests. They still get static checks and lint.
5. **Lockfile** → the packages whose resolved installs changed, then their consumers. Root importer, settings, overrides, patches → everything. Catalog-only workspace edits → nothing of their own.
6. **Package edits** → the package and its transitive consumers, from manifests plus names in imports, build commands and config paths. The deepest containing package owns a file. Cycles end at a fixed point.
7. **Test-only edits** (tests, `testing/` helpers no manifest exports) → only the tests that run them.
8. **Entry points** (`entryScoped`): a dependent of a shared library runs only its tests that load an entry exporting a changed module.
9. **Near**, with `--near`, for one integration-heavy package: tests the change edited, tests whose imports reach it climbing upward but **stopping at modules with more than 20 importers**, tests named for the changed modules, and **explicit coverage declarations** (`nearCovers`) for tests that read files from disk or run generated bundles.
10. **Covered-only** (`coveredOnly`), with `--near`: heavy proofs run on a PR only if it touches their covered paths, **even when it otherwise selects everything**.
11. **Own-job files** (`ownJob`: real containers, proofs), printed as `own_jobs=`: see [container-test reach](../../../../templates/plan/README.md#container-test-reach).
12. **Anything unknown** → everything.

Before shipping a rule change, replay it over historical diffs and compare the selection (guide section 4, "Verify the selector like production code").

### Left out of the reference

- Our repo's coverage tables, contract-vector and bundle-consumer rules: write yours as `nearCovers` and `coveredOnly` entries.
- The local mode (`--local`) that picks tests near the working tree for a pre-push command: build it from `changed-files.ts` and the same rules if you want one (guide section 14).
